summary: MSVC CRT stack probe (_alloca_probe). Walks the stack pointer downward in 4096-byte strides while the requested allocation size a1 is at least 0x1000, touching each intervening page so the OS guard pages fire for large stack-frame growth. Returns via the bare retn that the original alloca call pushed, so it restores control directly to the caller of the prologue sequence. Called by twenty stack-heavy functions across camera, config parsing, physics init, season data, and telemetry paths.

operations.description: Seed the probe pointer i from the address of the local a2 slot, i.e. the current stack high-water mark just below the caller's frame.
Loop guard: only while a1 (remaining allocation size) is >= 0x1000 does the probe keep touching pages; any residual below one page needs no further guard-page touch.
Per-iteration probe: decrement the pointer i by 4096 and reduce a1 by 4096, so each 4096-byte segment of the growing frame is visited exactly once.
Bare retn: returns to the address pushed by the alloca call site rather than a C-level return; no value is returned in the usual sense.

unresolved: The 4096-byte step is taken from the 0x1000 literal in the raw source; the actual OS page size and guard-page interaction are not visible in this packet.
The probe's effect on the exception-handler chain (_except_handler3 in this binary) is not recoverable from the raw body alone.
